themes_detail.label: Street noise surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from streets and sidewalks spiked to 32 this week—178% above the 11.5-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting a sudden deterioration in outdoor noise conditions across Park Slope/Carroll Gardens.
evidence: 32 street/sidewalk noise complaints this week vs. 11.5-complaint 8-week average (z-score: 5.25)
178% increase represents statistically significant spike (severity: high)
No prior Reddit or community board context available; emergence appears sudden
reporting_angles: Canvas affected blocks (Prospect Park West, Flatbush Ave, etc.) to identify noise source: construction, deliveries, outdoor events, or vehicle traffic
Cross-reference with DOB permits: 1,199 filings in 90 days (731 alterations) may explain construction noise; narrow to this week's permits

themes_detail.label: Dead animals piling up
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints skyrocketed 878% last week to 11 complaints versus a 1.1-complaint 8-week average—a dramatic public health and sanitation signal that warrants immediate investigation into disposal protocols or wildlife die-offs.
evidence: 11 dead animal complaints last week vs. 1.1-complaint 8-week baseline (z-score: 12.65, severity: high)
878% spike is the highest z-score anomaly in the dataset
Clustering suggests concentrated incident rather than random distribution; reporting timeline supports investigative urgency
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY and Parks Dept: what triggered the spike? Disease outbreak, environmental toxin, or seasonal die-off?
Interview residents on blocks with multiple complaints; map clusters to identify hotspots (parks, waterfront, specific streets)

themes_detail.label: Outdoor dining complaints explode
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints spiked 2,300% this week with 3 complaints versus a 0.1-complaint 8-week average—an unexpected reversal in a traditionally celebrated neighborhood amenity suggesting enforcement or operational issues.
evidence: 3 outdoor dining complaints this week vs. 0.1-complaint 8-week baseline (z-score: 8.69, severity: high)
2,300% increase is a relative extreme, though absolute volume remains low
Timing aligns with April weather; 'I Love My Park Day' registration opened 2026-04-03—outdoor dining season ramping up
reporting_angles: What triggered complaints? Noise, sidewalk obstruction, sanitation, or new enforcement actions by Parks/DOH?
Identify which restaurants or blocks; interview operators and neighbors to understand the sudden friction

themes_detail.label: Abandoned bikes pile up
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints surged 540% last week to 8 complaints versus a 1.2-complaint 8-week average—indicating either a new disposal problem or enforcement gap as warmer weather arrives.
evidence: 8 abandoned bike complaints last week vs. 1.2-complaint 8-week baseline (z-score: 6.19, severity: high)
540% spike suggests concentrated incident or new pattern; timing coincides with spring bike season
No supporting Reddit or community board discussion; enforcement angle unclear
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Dept and local precincts: are abandoned bikes being removed faster, or accumulating in specific areas (subway entrances, parks)?
Map complaints to bike share docking stations and park racks; are there storage or maintenance issues?

themes_detail.label: Sanitation crisis deepens
themes_detail.summary: Dirty condition complaints hit 66 three weeks ago—226% above the 20.2-complaint 8-week average—alongside elevated abandoned bike (8), dead animal (11), and overgrown tree complaints (7 last week), signaling a broader cleanliness crisis across the district.
evidence: Dirty condition complaints: 66 three weeks ago vs. 20.2-complaint 8-week baseline (z-score: 4.93, severity: high)
Converging spikes: dead animals (878%), overgrown trees (367%), abandoned bikes (540%), and dirty conditions (226%) all elevated simultaneously
Community board repeatedly requests park safety/security and park renovation funding—suggesting chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Investigate Parks Dept staffing, budget cuts, and maintenance schedules; have cleaning crews been reduced?
Feature: walk major park corridors and residential blocks; interview residents on perception of neighborhood decline and city response times
